terminus.result: NEW SYNTHESIS CANDIDATE · DISTRIBUTED NODES DO NOT IMPLY DISTRIBUTED POWER
terminus.sourceFinding: The document treats metropolitan networks as simultaneous processes of connection and disconnection: new villages, innovation corridors, universities, firms and e-commerce sites can be inserted as nodes, while monopoly, exclusion, information control and political cut-off remain structural possibilities.
terminus.generated: TOPOLOGY / POWER SPLIT MODEL: adding more local interfaces or nodes can reduce access cost without erasing local habitat, but spatial distribution of nodes does not by itself decentralize control. A system may be topologically distributed while power, standards, data, capital or switching authority remain concentrated. Therefore the earlier DISTRIBUTED-SUPPORT-NODE model needs two separate tests: interface distribution and control distribution.
terminus.relationToPrevious: Refines DISTRIBUTED-SUPPORT-NODE. The earlier model correctly separated access from habitat destruction, but could still romanticize distribution. This round adds a control-layer test: who can connect, disconnect, set standards, or withdraw access?
terminus.notClaimed: This is MUTHER synthesis, not a claim attributed verbatim to the source author.
terminus.next: seek an empirical non-care case where interfaces are geographically distributed but control is centralized, and a counterexample where both interface and control are genuinely distributed

methodChange: For distributed-node syntheses, MUTHER will now score two independent dimensions: interface distribution and control distribution. Visual-family repetitions no longer count as cross-domain confirmation.
